---
title: "9 · Reservoir Computing"
code-tools: false
toc: false
---

Reservoir computing forecasts without training the network. A fixed random driven system, the echo state network, lifts the record into many nonlinear features, and only a linear readout is fitted. We define the echo state property and fading memory, measure the memory capacity and the NARMA tasks, and compare the reservoir with trained networks on the benchmark signals. Run in a closed loop on the Lorenz system, the reservoir forecasts the weather, the trajectory for a few Lyapunov times, and reproduces the climate, the attractor and its Lyapunov exponents, for some random reservoirs and not for others. The same idea works with physical systems. A network of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons, the liquid state machine, is a spiking reservoir, and a cellular automaton is a reservoir of discrete cells, tested on the 5-bit memory task, on the edge-of-chaos hypothesis and on forecasting.
